sn8.5:2.1: While this sounds like a standard teaching, it is only found in this context. A different set of five factors is at [an5.198]().
sn8.5:7.1: This line is said to be an “ancient teaching”, and “undying word” (_amatā vācā_) is indeed found in Vedic context (eg. Jaimini Gṛhyasūtra 2.1, Brahma Purāṇa 219.58), where it means speech that is immortal since it is of the Divine. The Buddhist sense is that the truth is free from death because the principles of the Dhamma are always true ([sn12.20:2.3]()).
